summary: Prompt human review is supported because the snapshot shows worsening nocturnal respiratory symptoms and reduced activity, followed by an emergency attendance for severe wheeze, marked hypoxaemia and inability to complete sentences. The acute episode was actively treated and may be reversible, so any priorities-of-care discussion should follow confirmation of the current clinical situation and should not displace acute treatment. No active advance or palliative-care plan is documented in the available snapshot.

The emergency hospital attendance records severe wheeze, oxygen saturation 84% on air, inability to complete sentences, and initiation of nebulisers, systemic steroids and controlled oxygen.
The 47-resource snapshot contains no documented advance care plan, DNACPR/ReSPECT record, patient goals, or palliative/hospice involvement.
